title: Support for Employers and Employees Affected by Requirement for Companies to Fairly Consider Flexi-work Requests
what_it_is: Support for Employers and Employees Affected by Requirement for Companies to Fairly Consider Flexi-work Requests

sections.label: Questions on flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Manpower about support for workers, business attractiveness and shorter decision timeframes for flexible work arrangement requests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower what additional measures are being considered to support Singaporean workers whose employer offer flexible work arrangements and remote work from potential job displacement, considering the increasing trend of companies hiring workers located overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether the recent guidelines mandating the need for employers to consider requests for flexible work arrangements will make Singapore a less attractive place for companies to do business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower with regard to the new Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests coming into effect, whether the Ministry has considered mandating a shorter timeframe for employers to communicate their decision on a request for flexible work arrangements instead of the two months' timeframe.

sections.label: Guidelines effective 1 December
sections.summary: The guidelines take effect on 1 December this year, with consensus not to mandate flexible work arrangements or set hard targets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The guidelines will take effect on 1 December this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The consensus was that we should not mandate FWAs or set hard targets.

sections.label: Employers must consider FWA requests
sections.summary: The guideline requires employers to properly consider employees' formal flexible work arrangement requests.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: What the guideline does is to require employers to properly consider employees' formal FWA requests.

sections.label: Guidelines set process, not approval
sections.summary: The guidelines specify a requesting and considering process but do not mandate approval, letting employers decide based on team, business and clients.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The guidelines specify the need for a process for requesting and considering FWA requests, but do not mandate that every FWA request must be approved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The guidelines allow employers to decide on the FWA request, depending on what works for the team, the business and the clients.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The guidelines aim to shape the right norms and expectations around FWAs.

sections.label: FWA guidelines clarifications
sections.summary: Flexible work arrangements do not mean only work from home, and from 1 December not every workplace must have them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: First of all, let me clarify that FWAs do not mean work from home only.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: And the final one: the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangements, which take effect from 1 December, would not mean that come December, every workplace must have FWAs.

sections.label: Guidelines for negotiation, not intervention
sections.summary: The guidelines give both parties a process to negotiate, with no intention to intervene in how companies decide FWA requests if a proper process is applied.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: To make sure workplaces continue to be productive and have harmonious workplace relationships, these guidelines actually are for both parties – as what hon Member, Ms Lim Biow Chuan suggested – to have a way, a process to negotiate and also to discuss what works for the individual, what works for the team, the business and the clients.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: There is no intention whatsoever for these guidelines to intervene on how companies should decide on the FWA requests coming from the employees, as long as the employers apply a proper process in evaluating and responding to the FWA requests.

sections.label: Guidelines for FWA requests
sections.summary: Guidelines to guide the conversation and implementation of FWA requests would be more practical and balanced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Instead, guidelines to guide the conversation and implementation of FWA requests would be more practical and a balanced approach.

sections.label: Singapore tight labour market
sections.summary: In Singapore's tight labour market, job vacancies advertised with FWA provisions attracted two to three times more applicants last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: In Singapore, we similarly have a very tight labour market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We know that last year alone, job vacancies that were advertised with FWA provisions attracted two to three times more applicants than those that did not.

sections.label: PMETs aged 45 to 60s
sections.summary: The Member asks whether guidelines and job scope redesign would disadvantage middle-aged PMETs and make Singapore uncompetitive, adding FWAs are not only work from home.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Would the Minister of State think that, especially in my Parliamentary Question, the Minister of State has not answered the part, with PMETs in the middle age group, between 45 and 60s, would the Minister of State think that this implementation of guidelines and the redesign of job scope would disadvantage them and make Singapore uncompetitive as a market to retain these PMETs?

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: I just want to reiterate that the guidelines which promote FWAs and tell employers they need to have a proper process to consider the request, do not mean that the only form of FWA is work from home and it also does not mean work less nor does it mean reduced productivity.

sections.label: FWAs, PWM and Tripartite Guidelines
sections.summary: If FWA workers' output and productivity are unaffected, there is no basis to reduce pay, and the PWM's spirit should lead the Tripartite Guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: For workers who are on FWAs, if their work output and productivity are not affected, actually, there is no basis for employers to reduce their pay.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The PWM was a carefully crafted, sectoral based wage which helps uplift the wages of our low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In the implementation, in terms of any form of guidelines, particularly the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests, the spirit of the PWM should really lead the entire thinking behind this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Flexi-time is one other aspect, and there is flexi-place.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Hence, in terms of the Tripartite Guidelines, it embodies a spirit of collaboration.
